transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-11-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Chen (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (Northwood CTO), Priya Shah (Product Lead), Evan Liu (Infra), Sofia Gomez (Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto gen): align on POC guardrails and bench plan, agree credit limit and procurement path.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do quick intros and then jump into the eval onramp, my name's Samir Patel, AE at Redwood Inference.
[00:12] Mark: yep Mark here, CTO at Northwood, excited to see the numbers.
[00:16] Priya: Priya - product, main use case is meeting summarization and real-time notes for sales users.
[00:24] Leah: Leah Chen, solutions engineer, I'll run the bench plan and shadow the pilot.
[00:29] Evan: Evan infra, I'll give the traffic profile and help with dataset access.
[00:34] Sofia: Sofia procurement, I'll be managing credits and PO.

[00:40] Samir: cool, quick agenda: workshop success criteria, talk workload size and expected tokens, propose a benchmark cadence, and then commercial runway - credits, terms, procurement. Any additions?
[00:54] Priya: want to make sure latency is sub 500 ms P95 for a 2k token request, that's kinda our hard requirement for in-meeting notes.
[01:05] Mark: and cost needs to be predictable - we have internal guardrails, otherwise this becomes a surprise line item.

[01:18] Leah: ok on the perf side, can you share typical transcripts sizes? average and 95th?
[01:24] Evan: average is ~350 tokens per call summary, spikes to 2k tokens for enterprise reviews, about 1.2 million requests per month in early prod - but initial pilot is smaller, maybe 10-15k requests over 2 weeks.
[01:44] Leah: that's helpful. For benching we'll include 2k sequence length scenarios to ensure KV cache and attention scaling is measured, and run both single-request latencies and sustained throughput run. We'll also measure cold-start vs warm-KV cache.

[02:05] Samir: on success criteria — propose three buckets: latency SLO (P50/P95), accuracy/regression (prompt-based evals vs your baseline), and cost per summary. Anything to add?
[02:18] Priya: also stability — no more than 1% errors or timeouts during sustained runs.

[02:25] Mark: timeline question — what's typical turnaround for benchmark and then procurement?
[02:30] Samir: benchmark plan can be executed within a week once we have data access; pilot run two weeks. Procurement / contracting — usually SOW plus procurement PO, customers are averaging 30-60 days; Redwood legal can speed up with standard terms.

[02:50] Sofia: for procurement we need a clear statement of work and credit cap. We can't run open-ended trials.
[02:56] Samir: absolutely — we propose a credit cap and fixed term. For this we suggested $12,000 in credits for the 2-week pilot, that covers X tokens at the proposed config, and a 60 day procurement runway to convert to committed capacity or an annual contract.
[03:14] Sofia: that's reasonable. Can you map credits to estimated tokens and expected performance?
[03:19] Leah: yes — we'll produce a slab showing tokens / estimated cost / expected latency across the model variants. For example, with our cur model (gpt-ish open model) at 8-bit quant and batching, we estimate ~0.8 cents per 1k tokens in the pilot config, meaning $12k covers roughly ~15M tokens, depending on prompts and batching. Note: these are estimates.
[03:48] Priya: want to lock in the model family and quantization settings for regression? We need consistent runs.
[03:54] Leah: correct — we'll pin a model version in the benchmark config (we'll provide sha/hash) and include a fallback model variant. We'll also pin prompt templates and eval sets.

[04:12] Mark: security — SOC2 and KMS, we handle PII in transcripts; need clarity on retention and encryption in transit and at rest.
[04:21] Samir: Redwood provides SOC2 Type II docs; for private deployments we have VPC and on-prem options, Key Management integrations (KMS/HSM). For hosted we offer configurable retention and audit logs. We'll attach the security brief.
[04:36] Evan: will logs contain raw transcripts or just hashes? We need to mask PHI.
[04:41] Leah: we can configure redaction pipelines and avoid storing raw transcripts in the test bucket; we can also show proof of process in the runbook.

[04:55] Priya: on benchmarking, what about cold starts — we need to emulate realistic burst traffic from meetings that start concurrently.
[05:02] Leah: we'll run ramp tests with bursts, sustained QPS runs, and prefix caching scenarios. We'll also instrument KV cache hit rates.

[05:12] Samir: any competitor considerations?
[05:15] Mark: we looked at Anthropic and Bedrock but they were either too pricey or didn't support our on-prem needs. Also evaluating OpenAI for hosted but uncertain on SLAs.

[05:28] Sofia: procurement nuance — if we go above credits we need an escalation mechanism and a PO amendment path.
[05:34] Samir: yes we can offer overage protection: pause at credit cap and notify account team; optionally enable auto-topup with pre-approved PO.

[05:44] Evan: what about dedicated vs hosted for the pilot? We prefer hosted for speed but want a path to Dedicated later.
[05:51] Leah: hosted is fastest to spin up; Dedicated reserved pools are ms-faster and lower unit cost at scale. For pilot we recommend hosted with a routing policy to dedicated if you'd like to test both in a canary.

[06:08] Priya: expected success criteria recap?
[06:12] Samir: P95 latency < 500 ms for 2k tokens (goal), accuracy equal or better than current baseline (we'll define eval prompts), error rate <1%, and cost per summary within your guardrail (we'll map to credits).

[06:27] Mark: agreed. Now legal — can we get a sample SOW and standard T&Cs?
[06:31] Samir: yes, I'll attach a sample SOW and standard terms in the follow-up email; Redwood can also accept customer-supplied amendments but that extends the procurement timeline.

[06:44] Priya: one more technical question — how do you handle streaming and function/tool-calls for our summarization AND action item extraction?
[06:50] Leah: Redwood runtime supports streaming tokens and structured outputs; we'll include plan to test both streaming and non-streaming to catch reassembly latencies. For tool-calling we can emulate your action-item extraction pipeline.

[07:05] Mark: cool. On the benchmark test data — we'll provide a subset with PII masked, about 300 sample meetings spanning short and long formats.
[07:13] Evan: we'll create a presigned S3 share for Redwood's bench harness.

[07:20] Samir: excellent. So immediate commercial guardrails: 2-week pilot, $12k credit cap, model/version pinned, bench runbook, and procurement path SOW -> PO within 60 days. Does that align?
[07:31] Sofia: yes, subject to seeing pricing slab and SOW.

[07:36] Leah: next steps to make it concrete: I'll draft the bench plan with explicit tests (cold/warm, burst, steady-state, regression prompts), Samir will send pricing slab and SOC2 brief, Evan will provision data access, Sofia will confirm procurement steps.

[07:52] Priya: one potential blocker: if latency misses, what's the remediation? Can we move to Dedicated test nodes mid-pilot?
[07:58] Samir: yes — we can arrange a canary to dedicated nodes if needed; that would alter economics but we can model it in the slab. We can also enable temporary autoscaling to handle bursts.

[08:12] Mark: want to record the acceptance criteria — please include exact prompt set and the regression thresholds.
[08:18] Leah: will do. We'll include pass/fail metrics for each test and a diff report vs baseline.

[08:26] Sofia: regarding billing — will credits be invoiced up front or net 30 after pilot acceptance?
[08:31] Samir: typical is credits applied to account up front or invoiced net 30 depending on procurement constraints; we'll be flexible. For pilot we can pre-apply credits and then reconcile in post-pilot contracting.

[08:45] Priya: curious about what constitutes a failed pilot — do we have an exit clause?
[08:49] Samir: yes — pilot acceptance criteria mutually agreed — if not met, there is no automatic purchase obligation. The SOW will capture exit / acceptance tests.

[09:02] Mark: good. This all sounds feasible. Any other items?
[09:06] Evan: just permissions and IAM for bench infra — we need a least-privileged role for Redwood bench harness.
[09:11] Leah: we'll provide an IAM policy template.

[09:18] Samir: ok let's recap verbally then close with next steps.
[09:22] (rapid cross-talk)
[09:30] Samir: recap — Redwood to send SOC2 brief, pricing slab mapping to token/run estimates, SOW template, bench plan; Northwood to provide sample dataset, traffic profile and confirm procurement timeline; schedule bench kickoff for 2025-11-27.
[09:50] Priya: agreed. Thanks everyone.
[09:54] Mark: thanks, looking forward.
[09:57] Sofia: thanks.
[10:00] Leah: bye all.
